guards.what: egg slot placement in the enemy list
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): Named encounter SLOTS are ported, and with them the re-sort that gives the enemy list its order. `CreatureCmd.Add` appends to `_enemies` (CombatState.cs:534-547) and then calls `CombatManager.AddCreature`, which runs `_state.SortEnemiesBySlotName()` whenever `creature.SlotName != null` (CombatManager.cs:841-851) -- sorting the whole list by `Encounter.Slots.IndexOf(SlotName)` (CombatState.cs:495-501). So a spawn's POSITION is decided by its named slot, not by insertion order. Shipped: `Encounter.slots` / `Encounter.monster_slots` with `get_next_slot` (`Slots.FirstOrDefault(unoccupied, string.Empty)` -- EncounterModel.cs:245-248, empty-string default reproduced, not smoothed) and `last_free_slot` (`Slots.LastOrDefault(unoccupied)`, no default, so a full row yields None); `Creature.slot_name`; `CombatState.encounter` and `CombatState.sort_enemies_by_slot_name`; and a `slot_name=` argument on `CreatureCmd.add` that sets it and re-sorts. Encounters with no row are unaffected -- the sort is a no-op and a spawn appends, which is every other encounter.  This site: Ovicopter.cs:87 takes `Slots.LastOrDefault(unoccupied)` against OvicopterNormal.cs:16's [egg1..egg5, ovicopter] under `if (text != null)` (:88), i.e. the OTHER end of the row. monsters/hive/ovicopter.py's `_lay_eggs` now asks the encounter for that slot and passes it to CreatureCmd.add; the row itself is the egg cap, so the separate live-egg count is gone. WAS: an INDEX computed as `min(i for i, c in enumerate(enemies) if c is self or a live ToughEgg)` -- always in front of every live egg, which is right only for a FRESH row. EXECUTED 2026-07-29, the case the index could not reach: lay three (slots [egg3, egg4, egg5], enemies [egg3, egg4, egg5, Ovicopter] -- unchanged and matching), then kill the egg NEXT TO the Ovicopter (game slot egg5) and lay again. The sim now produces [egg1, egg2, egg3, egg4, egg5, ovicopter], refilling egg5 IN PLACE at enemy index 4 -- where it used to put the new egg at index 2. A full row now lays nothing, which is the `text != null` skip. FOUR LEGACY TESTS MOVED (non-negotiable 5, reason inline on the class): test_hive.py's TestOvicopter drove `fresh_with(Ovicopter)`, a synthetic one-monster Encounter with NO slot row, and now drives OVICOPTER_NORMAL -- which is both what the game does (the Ovicopter exists only in OvicopterNormal) and what those assertions were always about. Pinned by test/test_encounter_slots.py. NOT CLOSED: nothing at this site.  The text it replaced read: NARROWED 2026-07-28, RE-OPENED the same day: the fix reproduces Ovicopter.cs:87's `Slots.LastOrDefault(unoccupied)` only for a FRESH slot row, because the sim's eggs must occupy a CONTIGUOUS run at the front of the list. CLOSED: the parity/legacy fork is gone and the first lay now matches -- Ovicopter._lay_eggs (sts2_rl/monsters/hive/ovicopter.py:128-152) computes `idx = min(i for i, c in enumerate(ctx.enemies) if c is self or (isinstance(c, ToughEgg) and not c.is_gone))` and calls `CreatureCmd.add(ctx.hooks, egg, index=idx)` unconditionally, so the opening lay produces [egg, egg, egg, Ovicopter] where it used to produce the Ovicopter FIRST. STILL OPEN: that index is always IN FRONT of every live egg, so a slot freed in the MIDDLE of the row is never refilled in place. The game picks the LAST free entry of OvicopterNormal.Slots ([egg1..egg5, ovicopter], OvicopterNormal.cs:16) and then re-sorts Enemies by Slots.IndexOf -- CreatureCmd.cs:68-69 calls CombatState.AddCreature (which appends) and then CombatManager.AddCreature, which runs `_state.SortEnemiesBySlotName()` whenever `creature.SlotName != null` (CombatManager.cs:841-851 -> CombatState.SortEnemiesBySlotName, CombatState.cs:495-501). EXECUTED 2026-07-28 against the real sim (CombatState(encounter=OVICOPTER_NORMAL, rng=random.Random(4))): the first lay gives ['E3','E2','E1','Ovi'] (matches the game); then killing E1 -- the FIRST-laid egg, which sits in game slot egg5 next to the Ovicopter -- and running _lay_eggs again gives the sim ['N3','N2','N1','E3','E2','Ovi'] where the game gives ['N3'(egg1),'N2'(egg2),'E3'(egg3),'E2'(egg4),'N1'(egg5),'Ovicopter']: N1 sits at enemy index 2 in the sim and index 4 in the game. LIVE main-line play -- SUMMON_BRANCH only lays again when alive <= 3, i.e. only after the player kills an egg, and only killing the LEFTMOST egg reproduces the game's order, so 2 of the 3 choices diverge. The observables are the ones this record already lists: index-addressed targeting, enemy turn order and the obs vector's enemy order. NOTE the cited probe cannot see this: `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b05.py ovicopter-hp` exercises only the FIRST lay, which is exactly the case the approximation gets right. WAS: the legacy branch appended, so even the first lay came out reversed. Rule 7: src/Core/Combat/CombatManager.cs, src/Core/Commands/CreatureCmd.cs and sts2_rl/cmds.py are cited without being hashed by this record.

guards.what: the three-egg loop and the five-slot ceiling
guards.rationale: C# loops i < 3 and skips (text == null) when no slot is free (Ovicopter.cs:85-93); ovicopter.py:130-134 loops 3 times and breaks at >= _EGG_SLOTS = 5 live eggs. Equivalent: slots only get scarcer inside the loop, so skip and break coincide, and 5 is exactly the number of egg slots OvicopterNormal.cs:17 declares (six slots minus the Ovicopter's own). A dead egg frees its slot on both sides - the C# predicate scans CombatState.Enemies, which a killed egg has left, and the sim counts only `not e.is_gone` eggs. Executed: the probe above lays exactly 3.

guards.what: MinionPower is applied to each egg after it is added
guards.rationale: Ovicopter.cs:90-91 awaits CreatureCmd.Add<ToughEgg> and then applies MinionPower 1m with the Ovicopter as applier; ovicopter.py:150-153 keeps the add-then-apply order and the applier. Order matters: the egg's own HatchPower is applied first (during Add / during construction), and HatchMove later strips every power EXCEPT minion.
